title: Invertible-view evidence frontier
hypothesis: Across a common frozen activation benchmark, invertible View families will produce a useful quality/invertibility/actual-byte Pareto improvement over linear steering and native invertible controls.
physical_object: frozen representation and invertible function parameterization
mirror_coordinate: per-behavior task code and family selector

development.selection_metric: heldout function error, inverse error, complete serialized bytes and active compute

fresh.reason: Source screens use different synthetic tasks, function dimensions, splits and measurement setups; pooling them would fabricate a matched benchmark.

storage.authority: actual serialized inference payload bytes from each source report
paid_objects: all reported transforms, bases, codes, task IDs and metadata

success_gate: A common frozen representation/task bank with matched code and mapper budgets; at least one invertible Mirror method must improve the actual byte/quality/compute frontier over both linear steering and its strongest native invertible alias, with fresh task identities.
failure_gate: NOT ESTABLISHED if source evidence cannot be compared on a common task/backbone or if required OFT/INNSteer direct controls are absent. FAIL if matched protocol completes and no Pareto improvement exists.
boundaries: This screening aggregates selected synthetic reports as separate rows and makes no pooled score or causal cross-method ranking.
No common frozen LM activation bank or trained INNSteer/OFT control is present in these source artifacts.
A follow-up matched benchmark is required before any cross-family Pareto claim.
